The Computational Research Laboratory provides a dedicated digital environment that supports all stages of the research process through specialized software and computational research tools. The laboratory offers access to applications for statistical analysis, data visualization, systematic reviews, scientific writing, reference management, grammar and language editing, graphical abstract and figure design. It supports undergraduate and postgraduate students, faculty, and researchers by enhancing research quality, productivity, and digital research competencies.

The Drug Development Laboratory supports teaching and research in the design, formulation, and evaluation of pharmaceutical products. It provides students and researchers with hands-on training in formulation development, preformulating studies, and quality assessment of dosage forms. The laboratory fosters innovation in pharmaceutical sciences by supporting faculty, undergraduate and postgraduate research aimed at developing safe, effective, and high-quality drug delivery systems.

The Drug Discovery and Development Labs comprise two complementary sections: the Drug Discovery Lab and the Drug Development Lab. Together, they provide hands-on training in compound screening, purification, analytical investigation, characterization, pre-formulation, and formulation across a range of pharmaceutical products. Students develop practical skills and scientific reasoning that connect laboratory data with therapeutic potential, product quality, and overall performance.

The MedEd AI Research Lab at Dubai Medical University is an advanced innovation and research hub dedicated to transforming healthcare education through Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning (ML), Big Data analytics, and emerging digital technologies. The lab serves as a multidisciplinary platform where medical education, healthcare innovation, intelligent systems, wearable technologies, and digital transformation converge to shape the future of health professions education and healthcare delivery.

The lab focuses on the development, implementation, and evaluation of AI-powered educational ecosystems, including AI Virtual Tutors, AI Virtual Patients, adaptive learning systems, VR/AR-enabled classrooms, metaverse-based collaborative learning environments, and intelligent assessment platforms. It also supports cutting-edge research in machine learning models for healthcare prediction, big data-driven educational analytics, clinical decision support systems, predictive analytics, smart hospital technologies, interoperability in digital health, and precision medicine.

A major area of focus within the lab is the integration of Big Data and Machine Learning into healthcare education and research. The lab works on analyzing large-scale educational and healthcare datasets to identify learning patterns, improve student performance prediction, optimize curriculum delivery, support personalized learning pathways, and enhance clinical outcomes through data-driven insights. The research ecosystem also explores wearable health technologies, Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), biomedical data science, and AI-assisted diagnostics.

Through collaborations with healthcare institutions, universities, and technology partners, the MedEd AI Research Lab promotes innovation in teaching, learning, assessment, healthcare simulation, and translational research while ensuring ethical and responsible AI integration. The lab aims to position Dubai Medical University as a regional leader in AI-driven medical education, healthcare analytics, and future healthcare innovation by empowering faculty, students, researchers, and clinicians to design and deploy intelligent, future-ready healthcare and educational solutions.

The Molecular Biology laboratory is dedicated for general molecular biology experiments, including reagent preparation, protein/DNA and RNA handling, and analysis using techniques such as Western Blotting and real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR).

The Pharmacology Laboratory supports teaching and research in drug discovery and development. It provides students and researchers with hands-on training in pharmacological techniques, including the study of drug mechanisms, efficacy, and safety using different experimental models. The laboratory is equipped to facilitate faculty, undergraduate and postgraduate research, fostering innovation and evidence-based pharmaceutical sciences.

The Simulation Lab is a purpose-built academic facility that supports competency-based, simulation-enhanced nursing education. The lab integrates high-, medium-, and low-fidelity simulation, immersive technologies, and authentic clinical equipment to ensure alignment with international standards in nursing education, patient safety, and quality of care.

Simulation-based learning is systematically embedded across the curriculum to develop clinical judgment, technical competence, communication, teamwork, and evidence-based practice within a safe and controlled learning environment.

The Tissue Culture Laboratory is a sterile laboratory for the growth, maintenance and testing of cancer cells and tissues under aseptic conditions. It enables controlled in-vitro studies, including cell growth analysis, drug testing, and molecular research related to cancer.

Dr. Zahraa Khalifa is an Assistant Professor of Pharmaceutical Sciences at the College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University. She earned her PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, with a focus on Drug Delivery, from the University of Strathclyde, UK, where her doctoral research focused on the development of multimodal vaccine delivery systems.

With more than 15 years of academic experience, she is actively involved in teaching, student mentorship, and the development of innovative learning approaches. Dr. Zahraa is a Fellow of Advance HE, reflecting her commitment to excellence in higher education. Her research expertise includes advanced drug delivery systems, nanoformulations, vaccine adjuvants, and translational drug development. With a Postgraduate Certificate in Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery, her research interests extend to the integration of AI and advanced technologies, including 3D printing, into drug discovery and development.

Dr. Amina Begum is a dedicated teaching assistant in the Department of Biomedical Science at Dubai Medical University, where she has been an integral part of the academic community since 2016. Holding an MBBCh from Dubai Medical College, she combines clinical knowledge with a strong passion for teaching to support student learning.

She teaches anatomy, physiology, and communication skills using interactive methods. Dr. Amina also contributes to curriculum development, coordinates anatomy lab sessions, and promotes interprofessional education among healthcare students. As a member of the Quality Assurance and Program Enhancement (QAPE) Committee, she helps prepare, review, and refine course files to ensure high academic standards.
Recognized for her empathy and student-centered approach, Dr. Amina is committed to creating a positive and engaging learning environment that fosters academic excellence and professional growth.

Previously at Kazan State Medical University, she conducted clinical teaching and research spanning medical education and pediatric gastroenterology, while contributing to curriculum design, and building assessment systems.

Dr. Ziganshina has presented internationally, including AMEE and the Canadian Conference on Medical Education (2021), and the Middle East & North America Higher Education Leadership Forum, International Educational Conference, Abu Dhabi (2024) and WFME World Conference (2025). Her scholarship focuses on assessment, internationalization, and educational technologies.

She leads Journal Clubs and CPD events on assessment, ed-tech, and internationalization, and serves as a peer reviewer (e.g., BMC Medical Education). A member of the EmiratesMEDs assessment sub-taskforce, she contributes to UAE competency-based guidelines, advancing medical education policy and practice.

Dr. Bassam AtallahAssociate Professor, Associate Dean - Clinical Affairs

Dr. Bassam Atallah is the Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs at Dubai Medical University. Prior to joining DMU he served as Cardiovascular Senior Pharmacotherapy Specialist at Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and Clinical Associate Professor at Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine. Prior to joining Cleveland Clinic he was on faculty as Assistant Professor of Clinical Pharmacy at King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences (KSAU-HS) in Riyadh.

Dr. Bassam Atallah received his PharmD from Bernard J. Dunn School of Pharmacy in Virginia and completed an ASHP accredited post graduate residency at Winchester Medical Center in Virginia. He was awarded the “Graduate of the Last Decade” award by his alma mater. Dr. Atallah is board certified in pharmacotherapy with added qualifications in Cardiology. He also holds an advanced antithrombotic management certificate from ASHP. Dr Atallah is a fellow of the Heart Failure Society of America (HFSA) and the American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP). He has several publications and presentations at national and international conferences. He was awarded the 2021 ACCP Cardiology PRN international award. His research interests are in various aspects of cardiovascular pharmacotherapy with focus on antithrombotic therapy, heart failure and hyperlipidemia.

Prof. Bazigha is currently a Professor and Head of the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls, UAE. She earned her Ph.D. in Pharmaceutics from the University of Baghdad, Iraq. Prof. Bazigha has authored a book chapter and over 50 research articles published in prestigious, peer-reviewed international journals, and has presented her work at numerous international conferences. Additionally, she serves as a peer reviewer for several highly regarded journals. With over 20 years of teaching experience at both graduate and postgraduate levels, she supervised many graduate students through their master's. In recognition of her contributions to the field, she was honored with the "Professor of the Year in Pharmaceutics" award by the Venus International Foundation in 2023. She has also been recognized as one of the Top 2000 Scientists in the UAE by the AD Scientific Index. Furthermore, Prof. Bazigha is an active member of editorial boards and regularly reviews several international pharmaceutical journals. She has been invited as a keynote speaker, chairperson, organizer, and scientific evaluator to prominent international conferences in pharmacy.

Ms. Hala joined Dubai Medical College in 2025 as a full-time lecturer in the nursing program. She earned her Bachelor of Nursing Science from Mu’tah University, Jordan, a Master in Pediatric Nursing from Mutah University, Jordan.

Her humanitarian experience includes serving with the International Medical Corps at the Azraq Refugee Camp, where she provided pediatric care in crisis conditions. In these roles, she has led clinical training, mentored students, and integrated digital learning platforms into blended instruction.

An accomplished professional in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Dr. Rana Sammour holds a Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honors) from Dubai Pharmacy College, UAE (2003), a Master of Science in Pharmacy-Pharmaceutical Technology from Ajman University, UAE (2013), and a Master of Science in Health Administration from the University of Atlanta, USA (2010, Online Degree). Dr. Rana earned her PhD in Science in Pharmacy (Pharmaceutical Technology) from the International Islamic University of Malaysia (2021), focusing her research on enhancing the bioavailability of Aceclofenac via a proniosomal system.

Since joining Dubai Pharmacy College in 2021, Dr. Rana has excelled in both teaching and research, delivering courses in Pharmaceutics, Biopharmaceutics, and Social and Behavioral Aspects of Pharmacy. Her academic contributions also include supervising capstone projects and curriculum development. As Head of the Student Affairs Unit, Dr. Rana oversees student activities, addresses concerns, and maintains effective communication with stakeholders.

Dr. Sahar Elnajjar is currently a Lecturer and Clinical preceptor in Pharmacy Practice Department – Dubai Pharmacy College at Dubai Medical University with over 13 years of pharmacy practice experience, including five years at Mediclinic Parkview Hospital as a Clinical Pharmacist, Dr. Elnajjar brings specialized expertise in infectious diseases, antimicrobial stewardship, and parenteral nutrition to our team. Dr. Elnajjar holds a Master’s degree in Clinical Pharmacy from Gulf Medical University and is currently pursuing her PhD in Clinical Pharmacy at University Sains Malaysia. She is a Board-Certified Infectious Diseases Pharmacist and a Board-Certified Nutrition Support Pharmacist, further complemented by an International Certificate in Pediatric Nutrition. Her experience in clinical research is evident through her publications in peer-reviewed journals and presentations at international conferences. In recognition of her contributions to research, she was honored with the “Achiever – Research” Award by GMU Alumni Summit in 2022.

Dr. Samah Anwar is an Associate Professor of Critical Care Nursing, specializing in Adult and Geriatric Critical Care & Emergency Nursing, currently progressing for promotion to Professor at Alexandria University, Egypt. She has nearly three decades of academic and teaching experience at Alexandria University, King Saud Bin Abdul-Aziz University for Health Sciences, National Guard Health Affairs (KSA), Sultan Qaboos University (Oman), Khawarizmi International College, and Liwa University (UAE). Her teaching expertise covers critical care, adult health, geriatric, cardiovascular and emergency nursing, research methodology, nursing ethics, health informatics, and clinical education, using simulation, PBL, and blended learning. She has published 27 peer-reviewed articles in Scopus and other indexed journals, contributed to 12 books/book chapters, and has four manuscripts under review.

Prof. Sathvik B. Sridhar is a clinical pharmacy academic and administrator with over 26 years of experience in pharmacy education, research, accreditation, and academic leadership across India, Malaysia, Australia, and the UAE. He has served in senior roles, including Associate Dean, Chairperson of Clinical Pharmacy and Pharmacology, In-Charge Head of Documentation, and MS Clinical Pharmacy Program Coordinator. His work has focused on curriculum development, quality assurance, faculty and student mentoring, interprofessional education, and strengthening the link between academic training and clinical practice. He has authored over 250 peer-reviewed publications, contributed more than 20 book chapters, published 9 books, and supervised more than 35 MSc theses and over 50 undergraduate research projects.

Dr. Shereena S. Lootah, MD, PhD has joined Dubai Medical University as an Assistant Professor. She holds an MBBCh. with Honors from Dubai Medical College for Girls, a Master’s degree in Medical Sciences (Microbiology and Immunology), and a PhD in Medical Sciences with a specialization in Molecular Biology from UAE University. She has experience in clinical medicine, medical research, and academia, including clinical practice at Rashid Hospital and DHA hospitals. Her research expertise includes molecular biology, immunology, cancer biology, cell culture, flow cytometry, and gene-editing techniques such as CRISPR-Cas9. Her doctoral research focused on the characterization of the long non-coding RNA PROINS in human pancreatic beta cells. She has also contributed to scientific publications and undergraduate and postgraduate teaching.

At Dubai Medical University, Dr. Khanday leads the university’s strategic transformation in AI-driven medical education, overseeing the development and governance of AI-based education and research systems. Under her direction, DMU became the first medical university in the UAE to integrate GPT-powered agents within its Learning Management System and to integrate AI in curriculum reform .She has conceptualized and implemented several institutional initiatives, including the AI Xcelerate Hackathon, AI Integration in Curriculum and Research Writing Pilot, and E-Tuesdays Innovation Series, promoting AI literacy and innovation across the academic community.

Her scholarly and leadership excellence earned her a nomination for the UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize for the Use of ICT in Education, recognizing her contributions to technology-enabled learning and equitable access to education.

Dr. Khanday is the author of Quick Revision in Anatomy (CBS Publishers, 2014) and AI and I: Basics of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Medical Education (2023). She has presented her research Nationally and continues to pioneer research at the intersection of healthcare, education, and emerging technologies.

Dr. Khanday has extensive teaching experience across undergraduate and postgraduate programs in medicine, nursing, and Pharmacy . Her teaching portfolio includes Anatomy, Embryology, Technology in Health and eHealth.

At DMU, sustainability is a core value that guides our operations, research, and community engagement — nurturing a greener future for Dubai and beyond.
Inspiring a Healthier, More Sustainable Future

At Dubai Medical University, our sustainability strategic direction is to inspire and empower future generations to advance human health, environmental stewardship, and sustainable development through education, innovation, and responsible action. We are committed to embedding sustainability across education, research, campus operations, and community engagement by fostering environmental responsibility, social equity, and sustainable healthcare practices.

Through interdisciplinary learning, collaboration, and evidence-based action, DMU prepares healthcare professionals to contribute to healthier communities, more resilient systems, and a sustainable future, while advancing our role as a leading healthcare university committed to the well-being of people and the planet.

Through initiatives ranging from native Ghaf tree planting and plastic reduction to energy conservation and embracing sustainable construction practices, DMU is building a greener, more resilient campus that future generations will be proud to call their legacy.

Our sustainability strategy aligns with the UAE's Vision 2031 and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint while simultaneously embedding sustainability literacy across our academic curricula in Medicine, Pharmacy, Nursing & Health-Science.

At Dubai Medical University, sustainability is embedded in our culture, guiding how we learn, lead, and serve. We believe that preparing future healthcare professionals requires more than academic excellence; it demands a commitment to environmental responsibility, social equity, and the long-term sustainability of the communities and ecosystems that underpin the health and well-being of current and future generations.

DMU Students Showcase Research and App Innovation at Khalifa University Longevity Conference

DMU Students Showcase Research and App Innovation at Khalifa University Longevity Conference Student from Dubai Medical University (DMU) presented an innovative project at the Longevity Conference hosted by Khalifa University,…

Student from Dubai Medical University (DMU) presented an innovative project at the Longevity Conference hosted by Khalifa University, demonstrating how student research can evolve into practical digital health solutions.

The project, titled “Colored Noise as a Non-Pharmacological Intervention for Sleep, Stress, and Healthy Aging: A Narrative Review,” was conducted by DMU studentNaba Hassan Hadi Almumareta and Aya Bchar Kanani from University of Sharjah under the supervision and original work on colored noise by Dr. Shifan Khanday Associate Dean of Research and Head of AI and Smart Education unit . The work explored how different forms of colored noise, including white, pink, and brown noise, may improve sleep quality, reduce stress levels, and support healthy aging.

During the conference presentation, the application was displayed on a tablet next to the research poster, allowing participants to experience how the scientific evidence could be translated into a practical digital wellness tool.

The project reflects Dubai Medical University’s emphasis on interdisciplinary student research and innovation, encouraging students to move beyond theoretical study and develop real-world digital health solutions. The collaboration with the University of Sharjah further highlights the value of cross-institutional partnerships in advancing student-led innovation in healthcare and longevity research.
